note: The walker's figure (doc 23, W5; approved October 21, 2026): Matt's Meshy model, split into a body and two arms in nTop and coloured per vertex by tools/figure-prep/prep.py (assets/figures/walker.glb). The rest pose is the A-pose: the arms hang down by the rig. Metres, y up, body +z forward, feet on y = 0. bones: name, parent, pivot (the arms' pivots come from the model's extras, so a new prep moves them). skin: where each part blends between bones, as anchors along a height (y) or along the arm (t, m out from the shoulder). hang: the arms' resting direction. gait: per pace, step length, foot lift, arm swing, lean and the rise and fall of the hips; wade blends in by the water's depth. springs: the hat tip, coat skirt and pack follow a beat late (stiffness per second squared, damping 0..1 of critical). eyes: the two ovals the shader draws on the head (rest pose), their colour, a faint glow after dark (cd per m2), blinks and expressions. poses: sit, kneel, feed, the arrivals, and the keeper's camp acts (crawl, drink, pitch, lay, strike, crawlIn, climbOut; see actsNote). All motion is drawing only: it reads the walker and never changes it.

straps.note: October 29, 2026 (Matt): while a made carrier is worn (the satchel, the basket), two straps are painted on the coat (figure-draw.wgsl), from over each shoulder crossing the back down to the carrier. In rest model meters (x left, y up, z ahead): from, the left strap's top (x, y; the right is its mirror); to, its foot on the far side; halfWidthM, its half width; backZ, painted where the coat is behind this z (the back, and over the shoulder tops); topY, nothing above this (the head and hat); colour, linear albedo; edgeShade, its edges drawn at this share of the colour, so it reads against the coat (Matt: more defined).

hatBand.note: The hen-feather hat band (docs/future/15 slice 2b; lib-figure-band.wgsl), painted while the kit wears it (src/world/kit bands): barred brown feathers round the hat's crown just above the brim. In rest model meters (x left, y up, z ahead): footY and topY, the band's foot and top; minR, painted only this far out from the crown's axis (the crown's side, not the head under it); crown, the axis (x, z); feathers, how many round the crown; barShade, the bars at this share of the colour; colour, linear albedo; quill, the quill's lightness as a share of the colour.

body.note: What the creature pass reads: the soft contact shadow (scaleReal sizes it, times displayScale), displayScale: the figure is drawn this much of the model (October 21, 2026: 0.737, so you stand 1.4 m tall, not 1.9 m, and creatures read larger beside you; the eyes, contact shadow and all the motion (gait, poses, ground under the feet) follow it, src/world/figure/motion.js works in body meters), the cloth's sheen (none) and the eye bones for a wet glint (none: the eyes are drawn).

gait.note: Paces by speed in body meters a second (the walker's speed divided by body.displayScale, so a smaller figure takes a longer pace for its size and quicker steps); stepM, liftM and the rest are body meters too. The figure blends between them by the speed it is given. stance: share of a stride a foot is down (each pace may set its own; under a half both feet leave the ground between steps). The walk (2.2 m/s since October 26, 2026, about 3.0 body m/s) has its own pace; above it the walk turns into a jog (3.9) and a run (5.7, the run of 4.2 m/s with Shift): a flight phase, more forward lean, a bent-elbow arm pump, and bobM below 0, so the hips are lowest over the planted foot and highest in flight (Phase 1 fix F11). October 26, 2026 (Matt: the calves popped up and the run bobbed): the jog and run take short, quick strides (stepM), a small heel kick (kickM) and a small bob, so the legs never over-reach and drop the hips twice a stride. walkTurnDegPerS: how fast the body turns while walking (turnDegPerS standing). tipDeg and carryDeg: how far the body tips forward setting off and carries on forward stopping, at that pace (see lean); wade blends toward its own.

arms.note: The walking arm swing's shape (the swing itself is each pace's armDeg). elbowForward: radians of extra elbow bend per radian of forward swing; elbowBack: how much the elbow straightens on the back swing, the same way; across: how far a forward swing comes in across the body, per radian of swing.

springs.note: The parts that follow a beat late. hatTip.accelGain: how far the tip tips back as you speed up (and forward as you stop). skirt.strideSway: how far the coat skirt swings to the side of the forward knee, per meter the knees are apart front to back; skirt.speedFlare: how far it flares back per body meter a second. pack.tiltGain: radians the pack tips per meter it lags the body's rise and fall; pack.rock: share of the hips' twist the pack rocks with.

lean.note: Leaning into starts and stops (walker gestures, part 1; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/lean.js): the standing lean (the pace's, or a little at rest) follows a soft spring, with extra pulls. Speeding up pulls it toward the pace's tipDeg (full at accelRef, body m/s2; the walker eases up at 2.5 m/s2, about 3.4 body m/s2); slowing down pulls it toward carryDeg (full at brakeRef), the body carrying on as the feet brake. stiffness per second squared; damping (share of critical) while moving, settleDamping once stopped, so the walking lean easing off as you stop swings back just past upright once and settles. The pace is read at the speed you were going, falling off over cruiseFallS. holdS (October 26, 2026, with starts of about 0.15 s): the push off is held, fading over holdS, so a quick start still tips the body.

look.note: Where the walker looks (walker gestures, part 2; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/look.js). The head turns up to maxYawDeg and tips up or down up to maxPitchDeg in all (a posture's and an act's tip included); toward a thing it tips pitchShare of the way, up to targetPitchDeg, so the face stays in view and the eyes look the rest; the chest takes chestShare of a turn and what is past the head's limit, up to chestMaxDeg. Both ease on springs (headStiffness, chestStiffness per second squared, never faster than degPerS) and turn walkingLess less while walking. What it looks at, first wins by weight over (1 + distance times distFalloff): kinds.focus, the thing you clicked or are about to use (held focusS); kinds.arrival, a creature that just arrived (worth a look for arrivalS); the fire, a creature close by, a find. Each only within its maxM and within frontDeg of straight ahead (never behind you). A choice holds at least holdS and gives way only to one switchRatio better; a passing interest is looked at for its dwellS, then left be for againS. sameM: how far a thing may move and still be the same thing. liftM: how far over the ground it is looked at. eyes: the drawn eyes lead the head (it starts headDelayS after them), shifting up to shiftM (m across the face, x and y) by how far the head and chest still are from the thing (full at fullDeg), on a quick spring.

roll.note: The dodge roll (Space; WASD, October 26, 2026; src/world/figure/roll.js), in shares of the roll's length (recipes/world/walker.json steer.roll) and body meters. tuck: fully curled by the first share, uncurling from the second; turn: the one full turn runs between these shares. Curled, the hips sit pelvisY over the ground, the feet footY under the hips and footZ forward (knees to the chest), the back curls curlDeg and the head tucks headDeg. The ball turns about a point pivotY up and pivotZ forward, on an axis tilted shoulderTilt across the back, so it goes over one shoulder.

clips.note: Matt's Meshy clips on our rig (October 26, 2026; src/world/figure/clips.js; made by tools/figure-prep/clips.py into file). paces: which clip plays at which speed (body m/s: the walker's speed over body.displayScale; creep 0.45, the wade 1.0, the stroll 2.2 and Shift's 4.2 m/s are 0.61, 1.36, 2.99 and 5.70), blended between neighbours, all in step; each plays as fast as the walker moves over its own stride, stretched by stride (the feet reach that much further fore and aft, so the steps come that much slower). The stroll is a light jog: on our 1.4 m figure 2.2 m/s is about twice a walking pace, and Meshy's walk would play at 3.4 times its speed there. easeS: the clips ease in and out over this as you set off and stop. roll: Space's roll is the clip's span (seconds into the cut roll) over the roll's length, blended in over the first inShare of it; the rest of the clip (getting up) plays out over tailS after, blending back out.
clips.shotsNote: C3 (October 27, 2026): Matt's clips played once over an act, a gesture or the kneel (clips.js shoot), in place of the code's bend: span, the part of the clip (s) played over the act's or gesture's own length (doc 23's speeds; never longer), eased in and out over easeS, at most weight over the code (gather's stoop comes on top of the kneel, so half of it), and only on mask's bones (the squat leaves the lantern arm to the code). The code still keeps the feet on the ground and the hands where they act (the act's hand keys lead), and the act's own lean, head tip and hip drop give way to the clip while it plays. liftClump (Lift with the shovel): Pull_Radish from the stoop to the pull's end. gather (picking up finds and gathering): Collect_Object from the reach down to standing again. kneel: air_squat's way down over ease.postureS going down to kneel, its way up getting up again.

footprints.note: Prints (W6): each step that lands on sand, or on bare earth and mud, leaves a soft print the shape of the boot's sole, darkening the ground by darkness; it fades over fadeH game hours, and is gone once the tide covers it. Not on grass or rock (minWeight: how much of the ground must be sand or soil), not under water deeper than dryM. Never saved: the island forgets you between visits. soleM is in world meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model). max: how many at once (the oldest go first).

grass.note: Grass underfoot (W6): blades lean away from the walker and press a little flatter: under the body within bodyM (sitM when sitting), and where each of the last steps landed within footM, springing back over springS seconds. World meters, set for the 1.4 m figure (0.737 of the model).

kneel.note: One knee down, worked out from the leg's lengths (motion.js): the left knee rests kneeM above the ground, kneeBackM behind the hip and kneeOutM out from it; the hips come pelvisZ forward over it (the weight forward) and sit as low as the thigh allows; the shin lies back to the tucked toes, the ankle toeM up. front: the right foot planted [x, z]. maxDropM: how far an act may sink the hips while kneeling. leanDeg, headDeg: the back and head lean toward the work.

hold.note: The pot carried in both arms (S5, K-26): the hands hold its sides in front, l and r (body m, the model's own size before displayScale: x left, y over the ground under you, z ahead), eased in and out over easeS seconds; they give way to an act's or a gesture's hands.

poses.actsNote: The keeper's camp acts (docs/future/13-keepers-camp.md 2.3; October 22, 2026), played by walk.act(name) and src/world/figure/acts.js. posture: the walker's posture while it plays (for presence and the view); after: its posture once done. keys: at t seconds in, kneel and crawl (0..1, how far into each posture), lean and head (extra degrees forward and down; negative leans back or looks up), drop (the hips lower, body m), arms (0..1, how much the hands follow l and r) and l, r (where the left and right hand reach, body m: x left, y over the ground under you, z ahead). A key changes only what it names; the rest carries on from the key before, easing between. The last key's t is the act's length, and walk:act-done comes then. crawl: the hands-and-knees pose crawlIn ends in, held until climbOut or a walk (hipDeg tips the hips, pelvisZ brings them forward over the knees). ease.actInS: an act blends in from the posture it began in; ease.stepLiftM: a foot that moves far as the posture changes lifts this high on the way, a step and not a slide.

dig.note: One press of Dig (docs/future/13 10.2, P2c; src/world/dig): both hands on the shovel (the right on the handle's top, the left lower down; the shovel's shaft runs from the right hand through the left), ready, bend over and raise the blade, drive it down into the spot with both hands, pull the handle back to lever, lift the spadeful, twist right to tip the spoil onto its heap, ready again. The feet stay put (Matt, October 25, 2026: hands only, bent over). About 2 real seconds (it plays in real time at any speed). twist turns the chest to the right (degrees).

liftClump.note: Lift with the shovel (P2g G2; src/world/sowing/planting.js): the hands on the shovel as the dig holds it, the blade driven in beside the plant, a lean back on the handle to lever it, then the blade raised with the clump on it and a look at its roots, and back to ready. The plant comes up as it ends.

gestures.note: A short gesture for each thing the walker does by hand (walker gestures, part 3; October 24, 2026; src/world/figure/acts.js), played by walk.gesture(name, spot) or by the action itself. The same keys as the camp acts (kneel, lean, head, drop, arms, l, r), plus yaw (the head's extra turn, degrees to the left), but a gesture plays over the walker's posture: its kneel takes the figure down at least that far, it never stops a walk or a tap, and a walk fades it out over ease.gestureFadeS. Given a spot, the walker turns to face it and looks at it first. gather: kneel, reach to the ground, pinch, bring the handful up to the pouch at the hip. setDown: reach back to the pack, bring the pouch round, bend and lower it onto the pile. takeUp: bend, scoop with both hands, lift it over the shoulder into the pack. heapHere: a small bend, the hand opens at your feet. empty: hold the pouch out, tip it, a little shake. lift (a log or stone, L3a): kneel, both hands under the edge, heave it up, hold while it is up (under-log lift.holdS), lower it back. feedFire: kneel, toss a stick in, both hands out to the warmth. netSet: kneel, lay the net forward with both arms; netLift: pull it up hand over hand. rise: getting up from a kneel or a seat, a lean forward and a hand pushing on the knee. stuck: a look left and right (walks: it plays on as you walk off, not faded). sow: planting and placing gifts on foot (D1a): the right hand dips to the hip pouch, then one quick flick forward and up toward the clicked spot, the seed leaving the hand at sowing.json flickS (0.32 s), once a click. make (S1, October 24, 2026): kneeling at the workbench, both hands work at its top (about 0.6 m): a twist with one hand, then the other, pull the binding tight, settle, and up; as long as cook.json makeS. steep (P2e): kneeling at the hearth, hands out to the tea pot's warmth, leaning in to watch it, a glance aside, for cook.json teas.steepS. sip (P2e): still kneeling, the cup in both hands brought up, the head tipping back to drink, lowered to the chest, a breath, a second sip; cook.json teas.sipS.

setClump.note: Set a clump in (P2g G2): kneel, a small dig with the hands turn and turn about, the clump set in, the soil pressed round it twice.

pushIn.note: Push a withy in (P2g G3): kneel, both hands on the withy, pushed down, a new grip higher, pushed again, the soil pressed at its foot.
